name: Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd
tagline: Rs ~12,700 Cr capital-goods / process-equipment fabricator (oil & gas, steel, marine, nuclear, defence) -- ~46% revenue CAGR, FY26 revenue ~Rs 1,300 Cr (+54%), near debt-free, large order book, marquee promoter (Madhu Kela) -- but ~55-60x earnings and no moat in fabrication / EPC
business_overview: Lloyds Engineering Works (NSE: LLOYDSENGG; formerly Lloyds Steels Industries) designs and fabricates process equipment, storage systems, material-handling and turnkey packages for oil & gas, refineries, steel plants, marine / port and nuclear customers, with a growing defence arm and technology tie-ups (The Material Works, BARC, TB Global). It is associated with the Madhusudan Kela (MK Ventures) group and has acquired a majority stake in SISCOL via a share-swap.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 1,300 Cr FY26 (+54% YoY); ~46% revenue CAGR vs industry ~1.5%
Revenue +53% YoY, net income +86% YoY, PAT margin ~16%
~Rs 8,000 Cr order book; stated Rs 10,000 Cr FY29-30 revenue ambition
~55-60x trailing earnings (Rs ~12,700 Cr mcap on ~Rs 200-220 Cr PAT)
fundamentals_narrative: Growth and balance sheet are genuinely strong: ~46% revenue CAGR, +54% in FY26, ~16% PAT margins, near debt-free, improving debtor days (92 -> 67), an order book several times revenue, and a marquee promoter group. The India process-equipment / capex / defence-indigenisation tailwind is real. The reservations are structural: heavy fabrication and turnkey EPC is a competitive, pre-qualification-gated but low-pricing-power business; the ~Rs 10,000 Cr revenue ambition and the SISCOL integration are targets, not delivered; and at ~55-60x earnings and a ~Rs 12,700 Cr market cap, the stock already capitalises the growth path plus optionality. A 10x from here implies an L&T-scale outcome.

verdict_headline: Genuinely fast-growing, near-debt-free capex-equipment fabricator with a marquee promoter, but ~55-60x and mid-cap size cap the upside -- 'neither', conviction Low-Medium
verdict_reasoning: Directional overlap with priority-1 themes ('forgings / castings / cap-good exporters', 'defence / aerospace manufacturing bottlenecks', 'gas turbines / power-gen equipment') via process equipment and the defence arm, but processed as an external lead, not a discovery theme hit, and the exposure is broad fabrication rather than a named bottleneck node.

four_box score 1.5 -> 'neither' (hard). tailwind yes (India process-equipment / capex / defence-indigenisation is a real multi-year driver with a visible order book), tam weak (Rs ~12,700 Cr mcap; a 10x needs an L&T-scale outcome), moat no (competitive fabrication / turnkey EPC, pre-qualification-gated but low pricing power), valuation no (~55-60x trailing, growth + optionality priced). Growth is strong, but at score 1.5 the 'neither' is hard -- no exception available.

Conviction Low-Medium: above Low for the real growth, clean balance sheet, order-book visibility and promoter pedigree; capped by valuation, size, absence of moat, a dead VP thread and the untrusted source. Re-check if a market correction resets the multiple or if the Rs 10,000 Cr path and SISCOL contribution start showing in reported numbers.
